claim_audit_results.claim_summary: European Fellowship with a six-month non-academic placement extension under CC-07.
30-month action: 24-month EF at ELTE plus six-month AgroVIR placement.
ELTE (Eötvös Loránd University) is the beneficiary and academic host.
Progression: Plant Physiologist/Agronomist to EO/Geospatial Crop Scientist to independent researcher.
Named competence gap: Bayesian modelling, spatio-temporal AI, sensor transfer, uncertainty, domain adaptation, decision evaluation.
Eleven host-to-fellow competences delivered as supervised practice plus named ELTE courses.
Bidirectional knowledge transfer: fellow brings physiology/agronomy/hyperspectral; host provides geospatial/data science.
Seven transferable-skill strands in the CDP.
Open outputs: protocols, validation split manifests, methodology, code where IP permits, model cards, FAIR metadata, OA publications.
Weekly 1:1 with supervisor; weekly co-supervisor session through WP3/WP4; monthly progress record; quarterly CDP review.
Co-supervisor leads methodology and QA for model development; fellow designs/builds/runs models.
CDP is deliverable D1.3, due M3, jointly owned, with six named components.
CDP progress is a tracked KPI (K11): agreed by M3, reviewed at five steering points, tracing to D1.3.
Distinctive profile combining biology, scalable geospatial prediction and operational decision support.
Fellow gains end-to-end pipeline experience: evidence to validated model to cross-country to commercial-field to MVP.
Profile relevant to European research institutes, universities, EU agri/environmental research and EO organisations.
Co-design/deliver an ELTE MSc EO-for-agriculture module unit and co-supervise one PhD field-experiment component.
Fellow taught five years at university level including syllabus design, lecturing, examining and BSc thesis supervision.
Four principal scientific outputs P1-P4 with at least two peer-reviewed submissions during/after the fellowship.
AgroVIR placement supplies inter-sectoral competences the academic host cannot provide.
Placement makes the fellow employable in precision-ag, irrigation-tech and FMIS companies as well as academia.
Placement content: operational hardening, structured MVP assessment, FMIS roadmap authoring, grower requirements/user testing.
The placement is assessed by evaluators in Part B-1 and presented as a career measure.
Measures instantiate EO-01 (skills/employability) and EI-01 (employability/career mobility).
International/inter-sectoral/interdisciplinary dimensions forge new mind-sets (EO-02).
AgroVIR is the non-academic placement host and external evaluator.
Dissemination targets four scientific outputs P1-P4, at least two peer-reviewed submissions, one OA article/year.
Outputs follow 'as open as possible, as closed as necessary' with named open outputs.
Training/dissemination integrate open-science, digital skills and knowledge valorisation as required by the call.
Hyperspectral-to-Sentinel transfer library (D2.2) released with transferable/hyperspectral-only verdict per feature (K2).
FIELDWISE predictive engine/model card (D3.2) released with a published model card (K4).
Hungary->Bulgaria transferability report (D4.2) and Adaptation protocol (D4.3, K6) shared with MVCRI/community.
Harmonised historical database (D1.1), month 6, curated FAIR with QC flags and metadata (K1).
One public field demo with AgroVIR farmers and one public-facing article/year; operator measure, no deliverable id, EI-03/EO-03.
Results fed into teaching via ELTE MSc module unit and PhD field-experiment co-supervision (EO-08/EI-06).
DrR web MVP (D5.1) delivered by month 24 serving stress probability, uncertainty, spatial risk, priority, temporal evolution (K7).
AgroVIR functional/technical evaluation (D5.4, nine dimensions, K9) plus Field Decision Value report (D5.3, K8).
FMIS integration roadmap (D5.5), month 30, names interfaces/post-fellowship steps (K10); named post-MSCA route (OC5).
MVP is the research-to-operation demonstrator, not the primary objective; full commercial integration not promised.
Outputs persist beyond fellowship as maintained FAIR outputs, reusable library/protocol, FMIS roadmap, MSc module; shared across partners.
Commercially sensitive AgroVIR farm data governed by a data-sharing agreement, published only aggregated/anonymised.
Exploitation/IP treatment answers the previous evaluation's criticism on route-to-users and IP substantiation.
DEC measures map to Tier 2B outcomes/impacts (EO-03/07/08; EI-02/03/05/06).
MATE, MVCRI and AgroVIR are associated partners.
Framework for agricultural AI judged by transferability, plus proximal-hyperspectral-to-Sentinel bridge (IMP-SCI).
Agricultural ML is predominantly evaluated via retrospective metrics (R2, RMSE, F1) that mislead operationally.
Scientific contribution and reusable assets advance EI-05 and EI-02.
~30% of EU territory affected by seasonal water scarcity in an average year, intensified by climate change.
Water scarcity produces yield losses and higher water costs; processing tomato is a high-value test case (IMP-AGRI).
Contributes to EU water-savings opportunity via better irrigation timing; no advance % claim, quantified from evidence (IMP-ENV).
Field Decision Value report (D5.3) computes decision value for two+ models with lead time, false-action, missed-stress (K8).
Desktop prototype to validated web MVP (D5.1, M24, K7), externally evaluated across nine dimensions (D5.4, K9) (IMP-TECH).
FMIS roadmap (D5.5, M30) names interfaces/post-fellowship steps (K10); research-to-operation path with named route (OC5).
MATE-MVCRI architecture investigates cross-European transfer of agricultural AI (IMP-EU).
Each impact route terminates in a named deliverable and a tracked KPI, so every contribution is checkable.
MSCA default IP: ELTE owns results, fellow author-inventor; open dissemination primary; protection via copyright/trade secrets; patenting only if AgroVIR eval finds protectable subject matter.
